project.objective: Did Georg Gajdosch of Lidečko, Moravia have a daughter Anna, baptised 22 April 1718 — and was her mother named Catharina rather than the Dorothea the tree records as his wife?

questions.question: Do independent records confirm or refute that Georg Gajdosch of Lidečko had a daughter Anna baptised 22 April 1718 whose mother was named Catharina rather than Dorothea?
questions.rationale: The tree records Georg's wife as Dorothea with no source; the objective asserts a specific baptism entry may name the mother as Catharina. The Lidečko parish registers (available via Matricula/FamilySearch) for 1718 are the direct test: a single baptism entry for Anna would simultaneously confirm her existence as Georg's daughter and name her mother, confirming or refuting the tree's Dorothea assignment.

search_stop.justification: Researcher chose to wrap up. The FamilySearch indexed abstract (ark:/61903/1:1:FMSZ-MBF) confirms Anna Gajdosch's baptism on 22 April 1718 with mother Catharina, corroborated by three sibling baptisms (Martin 1714, Catharina 1722, Zuzana 1729) all naming the same Catharina, against Joannes's baptism (Oct 1714) naming Dorothea — the best evidence gathered supports two distinct Georg Gajdosch men / two wives. By researcher choice, the original register images were not viewed: the browse-only original baptism register (vol. 2504, image group 005387300) was skipped once the indexed abstract returned a positive match; the Opava Archive's independent scan of the same volume (digi.archives.cz) was likewise skipped; and the browse-only marriage register (vol. 2506, image group 005387302, 1709-1779) that could independently confirm which wife(s) Georg Gajdosch had was never browsed frame-by-frame (only a nil indexed marriage search was run). Status left in_progress; this is a resource-exhaustion stop, not a proof.

not_reached.description: Image browse of the Lidečko baptism register, vol. 2504 (image group 005387300, 1707-1742), skipped by researcher choice once the FamilySearch indexed abstract returned Anna's baptism; the original handwritten entry for Anna (22 Apr 1718) and the three other Catharina-mother baptisms was never viewed to confirm the mother's name against transcription error.

Browse of the Opava Archive portal (digi.archives.cz) scan of the same vol. 2504 baptism register under Lidečko or Klein Litsch, skipped for the same reason — an independent image source for the same decisive entries, never viewed.

Browse of the Lidečko marriage register, vol. 2506 (image group 005387302, 1709-1779) — only a name-indexed marriage search was run (nil results); the browse-only original register, which could directly confirm whether Georg Gajdosch married Catharina, Dorothea, or both sequentially, was never browsed frame by frame.

items.rationale: The loc_001 locality entry and the delegation briefing identify FamilySearch collection 1804263 (Czech Republic, Church Books, 1552–1981) as name-searchable and the first search to attempt. A name search for Anna Gajdosch — and spelling variants Gajdos and Gaidosch — baptised in Lidečko in 1718 may surface the entry directly and name the mother in Latin genitive (Catharinae or Dorotheae). Searching Georg Gajdosch as father is also worth running to retrieve all indexed entries for his children, enabling a comparison across baptisms. Name-searchable per the delegation briefing.

If the indexed search (pli_001) returns nothing, the 1707–1742 Lidečko baptism register (image group 005387300, vol. 2504) must be browsed page by page. The loc_001 entry confirms this volume is the precise source for a 22 April 1718 baptism. The Latin genitive forms Catharinae and Dorotheae will distinguish the mothers. Browsing should also cover the 26 Oct 1714 Joannes Gajdosch entry — in the same volume and recorded in the tree without any source — to compare the mother's name across two of Georg's children's baptisms. The surrounding villages (Horní Lideč, Pulčín, Střelná) also filed their baptisms in this register; any entry for Georg near those villages should not be overlooked. browse-only (personCount 0).
items.skip_reason: pli_001's indexed search returned an abstract confirming Anna Gajdosch baptised 22 April 1718 with mother Catharina; the image-browse fallback was never needed.

items.rationale: The tree records Georg's marriage to Dorothea c. 1710 with no source attached. A marriage entry in the Lidečko parish register naming his wife would confirm whether she was recorded as Dorothea or Catharina — evidence independent of the baptism entries that could resolve whether the name discrepancy reflects two different women or a recording variant. Search collection 1804263 by name first (name-searchable); if not found, browse the marriage section of the Opava Archive Church Books (collection 1475346, browse-only (personCount 0)). The date range is set to 1705–1715 to bracket the c. 1710 estimate and account for the register's 1707 start.

hypotheses.claim: Subject Georg Gajdosch (K69J-F7Y) of Lidečko, Moravia, is the Georg who married Dorothea (KZYF-GBJ) and was the father of Joannes Gajdosch (K8GQ-C6M), baptised 26 October 1714 with mother Dorothea (ark:/61903/1:1:FMS8-XFQ). This is the existing tree assignment and is treated as a lead until verified.
hypotheses.notes: Competes with the Catharina hypothesis for the same subject. Source of the tree link (Dorothea as wife, Joannes as child) is an uncited compiled tree entry, so it is a lead, not evidence. No assertions extracted yet. Evidence to test: the Joannes baptism entry itself (father and mother named as Georg and Dorothea); whether a second Georg Gajdosch appears in Lidečko baptisms in 1714-1729 with mother Catharina. Under this hypothesis the Catharina-mother baptisms (Martin 3 Nov 1714, Anna 22 Apr 1718, Catharina 11 Oct 1722, Zuzana 9 Feb 1729) would have to belong to a different Georg, which is the basis of H2 and the eight-day gap argument (Joannes 26 Oct 1714 vs Martin 3 Nov 1714 cannot share a mother, so two Georgs were active at once). Any Dorothea-mother entry after 1714 that is not Joannes would weaken this hypothesis.

hypotheses.claim: Subject Georg Gajdosch (K69J-F7Y) of Lidečko, Moravia, is the Georg who married Catharina (surname and tree identity not yet established) and was the father of Anna (baptised 22 April 1718, mother Catharina), Martin (baptised 3 November 1714, mother Catharina), Catharina (baptised 11 October 1722, mother Catharina) and Zuzana (baptised 9 February 1729, mother Catharina). Under this hypothesis the tree's assignment of Dorothea (KZYF-GBJ) as the subject's wife and of Joannes (K8GQ-C6M) as his child is wrong.

The four Catharina-mother baptisms come from a FamilySearch search of collection 1784129 (log_022-log_027), with the Anna entry the one named in the research objective. Key test: the Anna baptism entry (22 April 1718, Lidečko, falls in the 1707-1742 volume, image group 5387300) must be read to confirm the father is Georg and the mother is Catharina. The eight-day gap between Joannes (26 Oct 1714, mother Dorothea) and Martin (3 Nov 1714, mother Catharina) makes the sequential-marriage explanation (Dorothea died, Georg remarried Catharina) impossible, so H2 requires a second contemporaneous Georg Gajdosch in Lidečko. That second-Georg requirement is itself an unsound-assumption risk until a second Georg is located in records; it must be tested, not assumed. Note: the subject K69J-F7Y is not yet tied to any Catharina record; the H2 claim is about which Georg fathered the Catharina-mother children, and whether that is the subject is open.

claims.claim: Anna was baptised 22 April 1718 at Lidečko, daughter of a Georg Gajdosch and a mother named Catharina (not Dorothea)
The Georg who fathered Anna is the tree subject Georg Gajdosch (K69J-F7Y), so that the tree's wife Dorothea is wrong

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Searched: FamilySearch indexed collection 'Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889' (five baptism abstracts: Anna 1718, Joannes 1714, Martin 1714, Catharina 1722, Zuzana 1729, all Lidečko), plus a nil name-indexed marriage search (log_001-log_027). Not examined, by researcher choice at wrap-up: (1) the original Lidečko baptism register, vol. 2504, image group 5387300 (1707-1742), which would check the index transcription of Catharina against the handwritten entry and may give godparents, residence or house numbers distinguishing two Georgs; (2) the Opava Archive scan of the same volume at digi.archives.cz (Lidečko / Klein Litsch); (3) the Lidečko marriage register, vol. 2506, image group 5387302 (1709-1779), which could show which wife or wives Georg married and would narrow the subject-identity claim; (4) burial registers, which would show whether Dorothea or Catharina died before the other children were born and what Georg each husband was; (5) no census-type or land/urbarial records for Lidečko were searched. Items 1-3 are reachable and would narrow the identity claim, which is why that claim is capped at possible.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Argument: Anna Gajdosch, baptised 22 April 1718 at Lidečko, and her mother's name

**Question.** Do independent records confirm or refute that Georg Gajdosch of Lidečko had a daughter Anna, baptised 22 April 1718, whose mother was named Catharina rather than Dorothea?

**Answer in two parts.** (1) It is probable that Anna was baptised at Lidečko on 22 April 1718 as the daughter of a Georg Gajdosch and his wife Catharina. (2) Whether that Georg is the tree subject, Georg Gajdosch (K69J-F7Y), is only possible, and the tree's wife Dorothea is neither confirmed as wrong nor shown to be right for the subject.

### Part 1: Anna's baptism (probable)
The FamilySearch index entry for Anna Gajdosch records a baptism on 22 April 1718 at Lidečko, father Georg Gajdosch, mother Catharina (ark:/61903/1:1:FMSZ-MBF). Stored citation: "Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMSZ-MBX : Mon Oct 19 23:50:27 UTC 2026), Entry for Anna Gajdosch and Georg Gajdosch, 22 April 1718. The source is a derivative index abstract of an original parish register; its information is primary (the parent presenting the child is the informant), the basis is stated, and the evidence is direct. Three further derivative index entries from the same parish name Georg Gajdosch with the same mother Catharina: Martin (3 November 1714, ark:/61903/1:1:FMS8-6GZ), Catharina (11 October 1722, ark:/61903/1:1:FMSZ-SFP) and Zuzana (9 February 1729, ark:/61903/1:1:FMSZ-9RC). Four entries naming the same couple make a transcription slip in Anna's mother's name unlikely, though all come from one index and no original image was viewed. Tier: probable, not proved, because the evidence is derivative and the original register and the marriage register were not examined.

### Part 2: Which Georg? (possible)
The index also holds Joannes Gajdosch, baptised 26 October 1714 at Lidečko, father Georg Gajdosch, mother Dorothea (ark:/61903/1:1:FMS8-XFQ). Martin, with mother Catharina, was baptised only eight days later. One woman cannot have borne both children, and a remarriage within eight days of a birth, with the first wife dead, is not a plausible explanation. The records therefore point to two men named Georg Gajdosch in Lidečko at the same time, one with a wife Dorothea and one with a wife Catharina. This is an inference from the dates, not something any entry states, and the unexamined burial and marriage registers could show a different arrangement.

The tree subject K69J-F7Y is linked to Dorothea and Joannes by the existing tree (those relationships carry no source entry in the project) and, in the research, by the Joannes baptism entry (hypothesis h_001). No record examined ties the subject to Catharina. Hypotheses h_001 (subject is Dorothea's Georg) and h_002 (subject is Catharina's Georg) both remain active; the index entries give no ages, residences or house numbers to separate them. So the claim that Anna is the subject's daughter is possible, not probable, and the tree's Dorothea is neither refuted nor confirmed. No conflict is registered, because the records do not contradict one another; they describe two families whose connection to the subject is unresolved.

### What the tree now says
Anna (I3) is linked as daughter of a separate Georg Gajdosch (I1) and Catharina (I2), who are linked as a couple, at probable quality from the 1718 entry. Whether I1 is the same person as K69J-F7Y is deliberately not written: the persons are not merged, and the subject's existing Dorothea and Joannes links are untouched. Anna's birth (22 April 1718, Lidečko) is marked primary.

### What would settle it
The original baptism entries (Lidečko register, vol. 2504, image group 5387300, also scanned by the Opava Archive) could confirm the index transcription and may give godparents or house numbers separating the two Georgs. The Lidečko marriage register (vol. 2506, image group 5387302, 1709-1779) could show which wife each Georg married. Burial registers could show whether either wife died and who the husbands were. These are reachable but were not examined, by the researcher's choice, and they, rather than more index searching, would raise either part. Like every proof, this finding remains open to revision if new evidence appears.

quirks: All surviving Lidečko church registers are browse-only images with no name index — must be browsed image by image. The baptism volume covering 1707–1742 (image group 5387300, vol. 2504) is the precise volume for a 22 April 1718 baptism event.

Records are in Latin and German for the early 18th century. Czech was not recognised as an official language in Moravia until 1905. Mother's names appear in Latin genitive form (Catharinae, Dorotheae).
No civil registration exists for the 1700–1750 period. Catholic parish registers are the sole vital record source. Civil registration began in limited form in 1874 and was fully mandatory from 1921.
The German name for Lidečko is Klein Litsch. The Opava archive portal (digi.archives.cz) can be searched under either the Czech or German place name.
Records are not available on microfilm — digital images only (confirmed by FamilySearch Catalog entry olib:2425382).
Lidečko served as a parish seat; surrounding villages (Horní Lideč, Pulčín, Střelná) also filed their baptisms in the Lidečko register. Entries for those villages appear in the same volumes.
The baptism register begins at 1707. No digitised Lidečko baptism records predate that year in this survey; whether earlier records were kept and lost, or simply never kept, is unresolved.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Lidečko, Moravia (c. 1700–1750)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **German name:** Klein Litsch
- **Administrative district 1700–1750:** Ungarisch Brod (Uherský Brod), Moravia, Habsburg Austrian Empire
- **Modern jurisdiction:** Vsetín District, Zlín Region, Czech Republic (population c. 1,800 today)
- **Economy:** Rural Beskyd-foothill village, predominantly agricultural
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic exclusively — Protestantism was suppressed and only legally tolerated after the Toleration Patent of 1781; no Protestant registers exist for this period
- **Archival jurisdiction:** Zemský archiv v Opavě (State Regional Archive of Opava), serving northern Moravia and Czech Silesia

## Boundary changes
- 1700–1750: Lidečko, Ungarisch Brod, Moravia (Habsburg Austrian Empire)
- 1918–1949: Lidečko, Uherský Brod, Moravia, Czechoslovakia
- 1960 onward: Lidečko, Vsetín, Czechoslovakia / Czechia
- Boundaries stable throughout the target period; search under Ungarisch Brod / Uherský Brod in the Opava archive system

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration in Moravia began in limited form for dissenters c. 1870–1874; mandatory civil registration was enacted in 1921 throughout Czechoslovakia (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Czechia_Civil_Registration). No civil records exist for 1700–1750.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers are the sole vital record source for the target period.

### Church records
- **Denominations:** Roman Catholic only (the sole legally recognised religion in Moravia before 1781)
- **Record types:** Baptisms (křty / N), marriages (sňatky / O), burials (pohřby / Z)
- **Surviving digitised volumes at FamilySearch:**
  - Baptisms 1707–1742, vol. 2504, image group 005387300 — **this is the volume for a 22 April 1718 baptism**; 142 images; browse-only
  - Baptisms 1742–1774, vol. 2505, image group 005387301; 225 images; browse-only
  - Marriages 1709–1779, vol. 2506, image group 005387302; 143 images; browse-only
  - Burials 1710–1762, vol. 2507, image group 005387303; 145 images; browse-only
- **Digitisation level:** All four volumes are **browse-only images** — 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable. No name search is possible; the researcher must browse frame by frame.
- **Originals held at:** State Regional Archive of Opava (Zemský archiv v Opavě). FamilySearch confirms: "Digital images of originals housed at State Regional Archive of Opava, Czech Republic" (catalog olib:2425382). Not available on microfilm.
- **Language:** Czech, German, and Latin. For the early 18th century, entries will be in Latin or German. Czech was not an official language in Moravia until 1905 (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Opava_Provincial_Archives,_Czechia_Church_Records).
- **Gaps:** Baptism records start at 1707; no digitised register survives for Lidečko before that date. Whether pre-1707 registers existed and were lost is not established by this survey.
- **Parish scope:** Lidečko was a parish seat. Surrounding villages — Horní Lideč (Oberlitsch), Pulčín (Pultschin), Střelná (Strelna) — are also indexed under the Lidečko parish in the Opava archive. Their baptisms appear in the same volumes.

#### Diocesan and decanate context
Lidečko falls within the archival jurisdiction of the Opava Provincial Archives. The specific Catholic diocese and decanate serving Lidečko in 1700–1750 is not confirmed by the tool results returned in this survey. The Diocese of Olomouc historically covered Moravia under the Habsburgs, but the specific decanate cannot be named from retrieved sources. For confirmed diocese/decanate assignment, consult the Index of municipalities of Czech Silesia and northern Moravia (compiled by Dr. Adolf Turek et al., published by the Regional Archives in Opava, 2004), linked at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Opava_Provincial_Archives,_Czechia_Church_Records.

### Census records
- **For 1700–1750:** No census records apply. Austrian-era censuses began post-1848.
- **Later censuses digitised:** Austrian census records for Lidečko 1880–1921 are online at FamilySearch (catalog olib:3371480, image groups 102030669, 102112429, 102198774, 102275237, 102339608). Originals at the Moravian Regional Archive of Brno.
- **Substitutes for the target period:** Domain estate records (urbaria) and tax rolls held by the Moravian Regional Archive of Brno may name householders; not confirmed digitised for this survey.

### Probate and court records
- Not confirmed in digitised form for 1700–1750 at FamilySearch. Domain and estate court records (vrchnostenské soudy) for the Uherský Brod district would be held by the Moravian Regional Archive of Brno.

### Land records
- **Land register (pozemková kniha) 1740–1881:** Digitised at FamilySearch, image group 104715679 (catalog: Fond C17 pozemkové knihy, vol. 11938). Overlaps the target period from 1740.
- **Stable cadastre 1828:** Digitised — catalog olib:4118204, image group 107201334; held at the Moravian Regional Archive of Brno.
- **Land Records, 1450–1889** (Ancestry / FamilySearch collection 1918632): covers Czech Republic land records broadly; images only.

### Military records
- Not confirmed as digitised for Lidečko at this period in this survey.

### Cemetery records
- Sexton records not separately digitised in this survey. Czech cemetery transcriptions: http://czech.stonepics.com/

### Newspaper records
- Not applicable for 1700–1750.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Declarations of intention and naturalisation filed well after the target period. Not applicable to 1700–1750 Lidečko.

### Tax records
- Not confirmed as digitised for 1700–1750. Estate records at the Moravian Regional Archive of Brno may contain tax-related listings.

### Other record types
- **School records:** Czech Republic School Registers 1799–1953 (FamilySearch collection 2328519, images only) postdates the target period.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch Catalog (catalog entry olib:2425382) | Baptisms 1707–1742 (img grp 5387300), 1742–1774 (5387301); Marriages 1709–1779 (5387302); Burials 1710–1762 (5387303) | Primary source for 1718 baptism; browse-only | Free |
| FamilySearch — Czech Republic, Church Books, 1552–1981 (collection 1804263) | Indexed records covering Opava archive parish books including Lidečko | Name-index search; may surface the 1718 entry without browsing | Free |
| FamilySearch — Czech Republic, Northern Moravia, Opava Archive Church Books, 1571–1905 (collection 1475346) | Browse images for Opava archive — Lidečko 1707–1905 | Lidečko church books | Free |
| Zemský archiv v Opavě portal (digi.archives.cz) | Same Lidečko church registers directly at the archive | Direct archive access; sometimes easier navigation than FS | Free |
| Ancestry — Czech Republic Church Books, 1552–1963 (collection 60254) | Church books | Alternative interface | Subscription (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60254) |
| MyHeritage — Czech Republic Church Books, 1552–1963 | Church books | Alternative interface | Subscription (http://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30248/czech-republic-church-books-1552-1948) |

**Coverage of this survey:** Volume_search returned all 5 digitised volumes matching Lidečko for the 1700–1750 window; the result set was complete (no further pages). All 5 volumes are browse-only.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Zemský archiv v Opavě (State Regional Archive of Opava) | Originals of all Lidečko parish registers | In-person; online images at https://digi.archives.cz/da/ |
| Moravský zemský archiv (Moravian Regional Archive, Brno) | Domain/estate records, stable cadastre, later censuses | In-person; some images at FamilySearch |

## Records NOT online
- Baptism records before 1707: not found in any digitised source in this survey
- Decanate or diocesan records (Olomouc diocese level): not confirmed digitised for Lidečko
- Pre-1710 burial and pre-1709 marriage registers: not found in this survey
- Domain/estate court records (probate equivalents) for 1700–1750: not digitised at FamilySearch
- Matricula Online and Archion: neither platform returned results for Lidečko in this survey; Matricula focuses on Austrian Catholic records and Archion on German Protestant records — the access routes for Lidečko are FamilySearch and digi.archives.cz

## Known record losses
No tool result reports a specific loss or destruction event for the Lidečko church registers. The absence of baptism records before 1707 may reflect either the parish's register-keeping start date or the loss of earlier volumes — this survey cannot determine which.

## Research tips
- **Go directly to image group 5387300 on FamilySearch** for the baptism register covering 1707–1742. The most efficient access path is the FamilySearch Catalog: search "Lidečko" at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog, click the camera icon beside vol. 2504, and browse frame by frame. This avoids the complex multi-level browse structure of collection 1475346 (per FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Opava_Provincial_Archives,_Czechia_Church_Records).
- **Search the indexed collection 1804263 first.** Czech Republic, Church Books, 1552–1981 at FamilySearch has name indexes that may partially cover this volume. If the April 1718 entry appears there, you are taken straight to the image. If not, the entry may still exist in the unindexed images.
- **Also search the Opava archive portal** at https://digi.archives.cz/da/ — enter "Lidečko" or "Klein Litsch" and select the N (Narozeni / baptism) register for 1707–1742. The same images are available but portal navigation may differ.
- **Language:** Expect Latin column headings and given names in Latin form — "Catharinae" or "Dorotheae" in the genitive. The Opava Archives wiki page notes the vocabulary: N = births/baptisms, O = marriages, Z = deaths (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Opava_Provincial_Archives,_Czechia_Church_Records).
- **Baptismal entries in Moravia typically include:** child's name, date of baptism (and often date of birth), names of both father and mother, godparents, and sometimes the father's residence and occupation (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Opava_Provincial_Archives,_Czechia_Church_Records#Parish_Registers_and_the_Information_They_Contain). The mother's name will be present and is the field bearing on the Catharina/Dorothea question.
- **Check the register index pages.** Many Moravian parish registers include an index at the front or back of the volume; image group 5387300 may have one. Check the first and last images before browsing sequentially.
